patient.chief_complaint: Sudden onset headache during sexual intercourse, vomiting, now 5 hours ago
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. Washington is a 55-year-old African American male with hypertension and a sister with a known unruptured cerebral aneurysm who presents 5 hours after sudden onset severe headache during sexual intercourse. He describes the headache as coming on explosively mid-coitus, reaching maximum intensity within seconds, rated 10/10, associated with immediate nausea and one episode of vomiting. His partner drove him to the nearest ED where a CT was performed and read as negative. He was given antiemetics and analgesia with partial improvement and was about to be discharged when he insisted on transfer here because of his sister's history of aneurysm. His headache has now partially improved to 6/10 but he continues to report neck stiffness and sensitivity to light. He denies focal weakness, visual changes, or loss of consciousness. He has no prior history of exertional headaches or thunderclap headaches. He reports his blood pressure has been uncontrolled and he frequently forgets to take his medications. His most recent BP reading at his primary care physician 3 weeks ago was 168/96 mmHg.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; photophobic; anxious
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm; EOM intact; no papilledema; no focal CN deficit
neurological_exam.additional: Nuchal rigidity present; Kernig positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Faint hyperdensity in suprasellar cistern - subtle, near isodense to brain
Very thin subarachnoid blood bilateral Sylvian fissures

additional_observations: Blood may be near-isodense in higher Hgb patient - but Hgb normal here
ct.impression: Very subtle subarachnoid hemorrhage with faint hyperdensity in suprasellar cistern and thin bilateral Sylvian fissure blood. Easily interpreted as negative on cursory review - hence OSH read as negative. LP essential to confirm or exclude SAH definitively.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 11.8 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 198 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.14 ng/mL (H), BNP 168 pg/mL (H).

special_tests.Xanthochromia: Yellow supernatant on visual inspection; spectrophotometry confirms bilirubin

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 26 cmH2O. WBC: N/A (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 158 mg/dL. Glucose: 98 mg/dL (serum 198, ratio 0.49 - normal) (ratio 0.49). Xanthochromia: Yellow supernatant on visual inspection; spectrophotometry confirms bilirubin.

ecg.interpretation: Neurogenic T-wave changes with QTc prolongation.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 6.2 x 5.1 mm with lobulation; no oculomotor nerve compression

output.impression: Right posterior communicating artery aneurysm (6.2 mm) consistent with ruptured aneurysm. Family history of aneurysm is clinically relevant. Conventional DSA for treatment planning.
recommended_actions: Screen first-degree relatives (sister already being monitored)

output.impression: Borderline mild right MCA vasospasm day 6. Monitor closely days 7-14. Maintain nimodipine and euvolemia.
Mild Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. EF mildly reduced. Supportive care recommended.

output.query: Familial cerebral aneurysm screening MRA first degree relatives

results.finding: Screening with MRA recommended for first-degree relatives of SAH patients (especially with 2+ affected family members)
First-degree relatives have 3-5x increased risk; screening detects 4% aneurysm prevalence

output.summary: This patient has a sister with a known unruptured aneurysm and now himself has ruptured SAH - constitutes a familial pattern. All first-degree relatives should be screened with MRA. Future children and siblings should be offered screening. Genetic counseling may be appropriate.

output.impression: Mild right MCA territory perfusion reduction without infarction. Consistent with early vasospasm. Consider intervention if clinical deterioration.

interactions: Metoprolol + nimodipine: additive bradycardia and hypotension possible - monitor HR and BP
warnings: Hold metoprolol if hemodynamically significant bradycardia

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from right posterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 2)

differential.key_features: CSF non-clearing bloody with xanthochromia; CTA shows PComA aneurysm
No prior headache history; CSF diagnostic of SAH
CTA shows saccular aneurysm not beading

optimal_actions.action: Urgent CT head review (request re-read by neurovascular radiologist)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Subtle Fisher 2 SAH missed at OSH
Hold metoprolol if hemodynamic compromise from additive effect

optimal_actions.action: Counsel family - familial aneurysm pattern; recommend first-degree relative screening

critical_actions: LP after negative OSH CT - clinical presentation strongly suggests SAH
CTA to identify and characterize aneurysm
Expedite aneurysm treatment to prevent rebleeding
Recommend first-degree relative MRA screening given familial pattern
contraindicated_actions: Do not discharge with diagnosis of coital headache without LP and SAH exclusion
Do not use NSAIDs for pain management post-SAH
key_reasoning_points: Exertional/coital thunderclap headache is classic SAH presentation - do not assume benign coital headache without full SAH workup
Family history of cerebral aneurysm in first-degree relative increases pre-test probability significantly
Negative CT at OSH requires LP - sensitivity of CT decreases after 6 hours and can be <95% in subtle SAH
LP with non-clearing bloody CSF and xanthochromia is definitive even when CT is negative
PComA aneurysm location is the second most common (after AComA) and classically presents with pupil-involving CN III palsy when large
Familial aneurysm pattern: sister with known aneurysm + patient with ruptured aneurysm = screen all first-degree relatives with MRA
